approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package of three bills that would allow the Commonwealth to recover costs for indirect biosecurity services under the Biosecurity Bill.

It would amend the Quarantine Charges (Imposition–General) Act 2014 to enable charges to be imposed for activities such as scientific analysis, intelligence and surveillance that benefit users of the biosecurity system.
The amount of charges and who pays them would be set in delegated legislation, allowing the Minister for Agriculture to adjust them to avoid over or under recovery.
Authorises the imposition of charges for indirect biosecurity services.
Allows the Minister for Agriculture to set charge amounts through delegated legislation.
Users of the biosecurity system, including businesses that benefit from indirect biosecurity services.

Introduced the Quarantine Charges (Imposition-General) Amendment Bill 2014, the first of three charging bills supporting the Biosecurity Bill package, explaining it continues current cost-recovery arrangements for biosecurity activities such as scientific analysis, inspections and surveillance without setting specific charge amounts.

Summed up the Biosecurity Bill debate, noting the Quarantine Act has been amended more than 50 times over 106 years and Australia's agricultural production was worth $53 billion in 2013 to 2014, and assured the House the Inspector-General of Biosecurity position and its funding, currently held by Dr Michael Bond, will continue.
